anchor.notes: Both reference benchmarks are old enough to be in models' training data to some degree (SWE-bench Verified certainly), so levels near the top compress as frontier models saturate them; the bootstrap shows that as intervals widening at the top, which is the honest behaviour, and nothing narrows them. When a licensed, fresh coding benchmark exists, it enters as a new anchor with a third reference column (`anchor create v2 --from v1 --reference ...`): the old reference difficulties stay fixed while the new column is calibrated, so theta keeps its scale, and the benchmark weights become equal thirds. Levels a user set never move in a migration.
